annotations.title: Core issues by status, ask, subsystem and topic

description:
Answer "which Drupal core issues match these filters". For "what should I review", call review_queue first: each of its buckets holds the arguments for this tool.
- With no filter: the open core issues that have not moved to GitLab, last changed first.
- The filters combine. A list filter keeps an issue that matches any of its values.
- ask: what an issue waits for, such as tests, a reroll or a review by a role. subsystem and topic: where an issue belongs.
- ask, subsystem and topic read the facets of the last daily build. They cover the issues that were open then.
- An unknown ask, subsystem or topic is refused with the three closest values.
- Row: id, title, url, status, priority, category, component, created and changed (UTC), ranking.
- ranking: from 0 to 100, the order a review queue lists issues in. It is null for an issue the ranking leaves out.
- Under a subsystem filter, a row adds subsystems: each match with its source, component or mr_files.
- count: every issue that matches. next_offset is absent on the last page.

any_status.description: true adds closed issues and issues moved to GitLab. The default is open issues only. It cannot go with status.

ask.description: Keep the issues that ask for any of these. The values are the slugs of the issue_ask_tag table, for example tests or reroll.

at.description: An RFC 3339 time. With one status code, keep the issues that were in that status at that moment.

follower.description: Keep the issues this drupal.org username follows.

min_days.description: Keep the issues whose current status started this many days ago or earlier. It cannot go with at.

offset.description: Skip this many issues in the same order. Pass the previous page's next_offset.

sort.description: changed (default): last changed first. ranking: highest ranking first, and the issues with no ranking last.

status.description: Keep the issues in any of these drupal.org status codes: 8 needs review, 13 needs work, 14 reviewed and tested by the community.

subsystem.description: Keep the issues in any of these subsystems, for example Views. An issue is in a subsystem by its component or by the files a merge request changes.

topic.description: Keep the issues with any of these topics of the issue_topic table, for example Accessibility.

name: list_core_issues
title: Core issues by status, ask, subsystem and topic
